newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU says still wants accord with US on Cuba trade.
newsitem.headline: EU says still wants accord with US on Cuba trade.

text.p: European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Thursday Brussels still aimed to negotiate a bilateral accord with the United States on trade with Cuba despite the naming of a WTO panel on the row.
In a statement issued in Geneva, he also said the two powers had "made good progress" in recent weeks in discussion on the extra-territorial aspects of the U.S. Helms-Burton law.

Brittan's statement was issued by the EU mission to the World Trade Organisation in Geneva. It followed naming by WTO chief Renato Ruggiero of experienced trade experts from Switzerland, Singapore and New Zealand to the panel.
The EU argues that Helms-Burton, which aims to restrict foreign investment in Cuba, violates WTO open trade rules. The United States says it is a national security matter outside the WTO purview.

"During intensive discussion with the U.S. administration over the last few weeks, I believe we have made good progress regarding the dispute over the extra-territorial aspects of U.S. legislation," Brittan's statement said.

Although there was as yet no outcome to justify suspension of the EU action in the WTO, he added, he was determined to pursue talks with Washington. "It will remain our aim to achieve a negotiated settlement," Brittan declared.
